```{r biomarker-selection}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# BIOMARKERS_TO_USE — whitelist of biomarkers used for filtering and imputation.
#
# Why this exists:
#   The patient-exclusion criterion ("any biomarker with < 3 valid obs is fatal")
#   penalises a patient if EVEN ONE biomarker in the input file is sparse.
#   When a downstream analysis only needs a small subset of biomarkers, this
#   throws away patients who are perfectly fine for that subset. Setting
#   BIOMARKERS_TO_USE limits the pipeline to the biomarkers actually needed,
#   so feasibility / exclusion / imputation / plots all act only on those.
#
# Usage:
#   * NULL         → use every biomarker found in the CSV (default behaviour)
#   * c("...","..") → use only the listed biomarkers; everything else is
#                     dropped from the df at load time and never seen again.
#
# Names must match the CSV column headers exactly (units included), e.g.
# "HGB (g/dL)", "PLT (10^9/L)", "CRP (mg/L)".
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

#BIOMARKERS_TO_USE <- NULL    # ← edit this: NULL = all, or a character vector
# Example for a downstream analysis using only 4 biomarkers:
# NOTE: CRP and WBC are included because the CRP-WBC discordance channel D(t)
# is derived from them (see the 'add-discordance-channel' chunk further down).
# Their presence tightens the "<3 valid obs is fatal" exclusion slightly — drop
# them (and set INFECTION_ADD_D <- FALSE below) if you don't want D(t).
BIOMARKERS_TO_USE <- c("HGB (g/dL)", "CREA (mg/dL)", "ALT (U/L)")
```

\newpage

# Setup and Data Loading

We load the longitudinal dataset of repeated blood biomarker measurements for
hospitalised patients. Each row is one blood draw for one patient, indexed by
`day` (days since admission, starting at 0). Static admission-level covariates
are preserved in the output.

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(splines)
library(patchwork)
library(mgcv)       # GAM with Gamma family + log link for skewed biomarkers
```

```{r load-data}
df <- read_csv("df_longitudinal.csv")

# ── Drop columns we don't want anywhere downstream ────────────────────────────
# - days_in_ER_capped : redundant with days_in_ER
# - ward_start_date   : not needed for imputation/clustering
# - solid_tumor       : kept solid_tumor_category instead (richer)
df <- df %>% select(-any_of(c("days_in_ER_capped",
                              "ward_start_date",
                              "solid_tumor")))

# ── Derive survival-related variables from the date columns ─────────────────
# All static patient-level except is_dead, which varies per day and is built
# downstream after the per-day grid is assembled (see df_main chunk). All are
# computed once here / there and then carried along like every other covariate.
# None of them are predictors of biomarkers and none are imputed.
#
# ──── INVARIANT: date_of_death is the SOURCE OF TRUTH ────────────────────
# All other death-related columns (discharged_alive, discharge_mortality_90d,
# days_death_from_admission, days_death_from_discharge, is_dead) MUST be
# consistent with date_of_death (and admission_end_date) as derived here.
# When the clinical registry's discharged_alive disagrees with what
# date_of_death implies, we OVERRIDE discharged_alive to match date_of_death.
# Specifically:
#   - date_of_death IS NA           → discharged_alive := 1 (alive)
#   - date_of_death <= adm_end_date → discharged_alive := 0 (in-hospital)
#   - date_of_death  > adm_end_date → discharged_alive := 1 (post-discharge death)
# The "<=" boundary (date_of_death == admission_end_date counts as in-hospital)
# matches the days_death_from_discharge sentinel rule below, so the two
# columns are coherent by construction.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   discharge_mortality_90d : 1 if patient died within 90 days of discharge
#                             (date_of_death - admission_end_date <= 90),
#                             0 otherwise (incl. patients still alive).
#   days_death_from_admission : days from admission start to death, as integer.
#                               -1 sentinel when the patient is still alive
#                               (date_of_death is NA).
#   days_death_from_discharge : days from discharge (admission_end_date) to
#                               death, as integer. Designed for post-discharge
#                               survival analysis, so the two non-event groups
#                               are kept on DISTINCT sentinel values:
#                                 -1  → patient still alive at end of follow-up
#                                       (date_of_death is NA). Censored.
#                                 -2  → patient died IN-HOSPITAL, i.e.
#                                       date_of_death <= admission_end_date
#                                       (diff <= 0). Excluded from a
#                                       post-discharge survival analysis.
#                                 >=1 → days from discharge to death, as a
#                                       positive integer. Event observed.
#                               Rationale for two sentinels: a single -1 for
#                               both alive and in-hospital-dead would force
#                               downstream code to recompute the in-hospital
#                               check from date_of_death every time. Keeping
#                               them separate makes filters trivial
#                               (e.g. `filter(days_death_from_discharge != -2)`
#                               to drop in-hospital deaths).
#   is_dead (per-day, added in df_main) : 1 from the day of death onwards, 0
#                               before. Always 0 for living patients.
#
# Manual data correction: patient c7663d22-d910-c301-bfde-3a1d24fc8362 has a
# recorded date_of_death that is known to be incorrect per domain expert. Set
# it to NA so the patient is treated as alive at end of follow-up.
#
# Defensive: parse dates to Date so arithmetic works even if read_csv left
# them as character (depends on whether the source CSV had ISO format).
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    admission_start_date = suppressWarnings(as.Date(admission_start_date)),
    admission_end_date   = suppressWarnings(as.Date(admission_end_date)),
    date_of_death        = suppressWarnings(as.Date(date_of_death)),
    date_of_death = if_else(
      patient_id == "c7663d22-d910-c301-bfde-3a1d24fc8362",
      as.Date(NA), date_of_death
    ),
    .death_minus_end   = as.integer(date_of_death - admission_end_date),
    .death_minus_start = as.integer(date_of_death - admission_start_date),
    # ── Reconcile discharged_alive against date_of_death (invariant above) ──
    # Stash the original so we can audit how many corrections were applied.
    .discharged_alive_original = discharged_alive,
    discharged_alive = case_when(
      is.na(date_of_death)      ~ 1L,   # no recorded death → alive
      .death_minus_end <= 0L    ~ 0L,   # died on or before discharge → in-hosp
      TRUE                      ~ 1L    # died strictly after discharge → alive
    ),
    discharge_mortality_90d = if_else(
      !is.na(date_of_death) & .death_minus_end <= 90, 1L, 0L
    ),
    days_death_from_admission = if_else(
      is.na(date_of_death), -1L, .death_minus_start
    ),
    days_death_from_discharge = case_when(
      is.na(date_of_death)    ~ -1L,   # still alive at follow-up
      .death_minus_end <= 0L  ~ -2L,   # died in-hospital
      TRUE                    ~ .death_minus_end
    )
  )

# ── Reconciliation audit ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Report (one line per patient) any case where the registry's discharged_alive
# disagreed with what date_of_death implies. This is patient-level, not per-day.
.reconciled <- df %>%
  distinct(patient_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(.discharged_alive_original != discharged_alive |
         (is.na(.discharged_alive_original) & !is.na(discharged_alive))) %>%
  select(patient_id, admission_start_date, admission_end_date,
         date_of_death,
         discharged_alive_was   = .discharged_alive_original,
         discharged_alive_now   = discharged_alive)

cat("── discharged_alive reconciliation ───────────────────────────────────\n")
cat(sprintf("Patients whose discharged_alive was overridden to match date_of_death: %d\n",
            nrow(.reconciled)))
if (nrow(.reconciled) > 0) {
  cat("Detail (one row per patient):\n")
  print(.reconciled, n = Inf)
}
cat("\n")

df <- df %>%
  select(-.death_minus_end, -.death_minus_start, -.discharged_alive_original)

# ── Covariate set (admission-level statics, replicated across days) ──────────
# Updated to match the columns produced by the Python pipeline, minus the 3
# dropped above, plus the 2 derived survival variables.
cov_cols <- c(
  # Admission window
  "admission_start_date", "admission_end_date",
  # Demographics & lifestyle
  "sex", "hospital_ward", "age", "pack_years_smoking", "alcohol_years",
  # Stay characteristics
  "length_of_stay_days", "days_in_ER", "ER_last_day",
  # Prior-admission burden
  "admissions_last_12m", "admissions_last_6m",
  # Functional / clinical scores
  "ECOG", "Barthel_index", "Braden_score", "CIRS_total_score",
  # Admission / discharge
  "admission_reason", "discharged_alive", "discharge_mode",
  # Tumor info
  "solid_tumor_category",
  # Death info
  "date_of_death",
  # Derived survival outcomes (computed above)
  "discharge_mortality_90d", "days_death_from_admission",
  "days_death_from_discharge"
)
id_cols  <- c("patient_id", "analysis_date", "day")
bio_cols <- setdiff(names(df), c(id_cols, cov_cols))

# ── Apply BIOMARKERS_TO_USE whitelist (set in the biomarker-selection chunk) ──
# If non-NULL, restrict the pipeline to only the listed biomarkers. Everything
# downstream (exclusion, feasibility, imputation, plots, output) inherits this
# automatically because they all derive from bio_cols.
if (!is.null(BIOMARKERS_TO_USE)) {
  missing_in_csv <- setdiff(BIOMARKERS_TO_USE, bio_cols)
  if (length(missing_in_csv) > 0) {
    stop("BIOMARKERS_TO_USE contains names not found in the CSV: ",
         paste(missing_in_csv, collapse = ", "),
         "\nAvailable biomarkers: ", paste(bio_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
  dropped <- setdiff(bio_cols, BIOMARKERS_TO_USE)
  df       <- df %>% select(-all_of(dropped))
  bio_cols <- BIOMARKERS_TO_USE
  cat("── BIOMARKERS_TO_USE active ─────────────────────────────────────────\n")
  cat("  Kept    :", length(bio_cols), "biomarkers\n")
  cat("  Dropped :", length(dropped),  "biomarkers from CSV\n")
} else {
  cat("BIOMARKERS_TO_USE is NULL → using all", length(bio_cols),
      "biomarkers from the CSV\n")
}

cat("Total rows:     ", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Total patients: ", n_distinct(df$patient_id), "\n")
cat("Covariates:     ", length(cov_cols), "\n")
cat("Biomarkers:     ", length(bio_cols), "\n")
```

```{r admission-covariates}
admission_covs <- df %>%
  select(patient_id, all_of(cov_cols)) %>%
  distinct(patient_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

```{r nan-percent-per-biomarker}
# ── NaN % per biomarker on the raw longitudinal table ────────────────────────
# Reported BEFORE patient exclusion so the reader sees the missingness pattern
# of the input, not what's left after filtering.
bio_nan_summary <- df %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(bio_cols),
                   list(n_obs = ~ length(.x),
                        n_nan = ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
                   .names = "{.col}__{.fn}")) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = c("biomarker", ".value"),
               names_sep = "__") %>%
  mutate(pct_nan = round(100 * n_nan / n_obs, 2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_nan))

cat("── NaN % per biomarker (raw longitudinal table) ──────────────────────\n")
print(bio_nan_summary, n = length(bio_cols))
```

\newpage

# Patient Exclusion

**Two criteria are applied (union, i.e. failing either triggers exclusion):**

- **Day range < 5**: the observation window is too narrow for any meaningful
  spline trajectory.
- **Any biomarker with < 3 valid observations**: if even a single biomarker
  has fewer than 3 non-missing values for a patient, reliable imputation is
  impossible for that combination and the patient is excluded entirely.
  This replaces the previous global `n_obs < 5` criterion, which did not
  catch the case of a patient with many total draws but some biomarkers
  completely empty.

```{r exclusion}
MIN_RANGE   <- 5L   # minimum day range (day_max - 0)
MIN_OBS_BIO <- 3L   # minimum valid obs per patient × biomarker

# ── Per-patient day-range summary ──────────────────────────────────────────────
day_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  summarise(
    day_min   = 0L,
    day_max   = max(day),
    day_range = day_max - day_min,
    n_obs     = n(),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

# ── Per patient × biomarker: count valid observations ─────────────────────────
bio_valid_counts <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(bio_cols),
               names_to = "biomarker", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(patient_id, biomarker) %>%
  summarise(n_valid = sum(!is.na(value)), .groups = "drop")

# Patients where the worst biomarker has < MIN_OBS_BIO valid values
sparse_patients <- bio_valid_counts %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  summarise(min_n_valid_across_bm = min(n_valid), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(min_n_valid_across_bm < MIN_OBS_BIO) %>%
  pull(patient_id)

# Patients with too narrow a day range
narrow_patients <- day_summary %>%
  filter(day_range < MIN_RANGE) %>%
  pull(patient_id)

# Union of both criteria
excluded_ids <- union(narrow_patients, sparse_patients)
eligible_ids <- setdiff(day_summary$patient_id, excluded_ids)
df_clean     <- df %>% filter(patient_id %in% eligible_ids)

# ── Exclusion breakdown ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
excl_only_narrow <- setdiff(narrow_patients, sparse_patients)
excl_only_sparse <- setdiff(sparse_patients, narrow_patients)
excl_both        <- intersect(narrow_patients, sparse_patients)

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("              EXCLUSION SUMMARY\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat(sprintf("Original patients:                        %d\n",
            n_distinct(df$patient_id)))
cat(sprintf("Excluded – narrow day range only (<%dd):  %d\n",
            MIN_RANGE, length(excl_only_narrow)))
cat(sprintf("Excluded – sparse biomarker only (<%d obs):%d\n",
            MIN_OBS_BIO, length(excl_only_sparse)))
cat(sprintf("Excluded – both criteria:                 %d\n",
            length(excl_both)))
cat(sprintf("Total excluded:                           %d\n",
            length(excluded_ids)))
cat(sprintf("Retained (eligible):                      %d\n",
            length(eligible_ids)))

# Show which biomarkers drive the sparse exclusions
bio_valid_counts %>%
  filter(patient_id %in% sparse_patients) %>%
  group_by(biomarker) %>%
  summarise(
    n_patients_sparse = n_distinct(patient_id),
    mean_n_valid      = round(mean(n_valid), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_patients_sparse > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_patients_sparse)) %>%
  print(n = 20)
```

# Prediction Grid

The grid is fixed at **14 days** (day 0 to day 14, 15 time points). All
patients and biomarkers are evaluated on this common grid.

```{r grid}
GRID_MAX  <- 14L
GRID_DAYS <- 0:GRID_MAX
cat("Grid: day 0 –", GRID_MAX, "(", length(GRID_DAYS), "points)\n")
```

\newpage

# Imputation Strategy


```{r manually fix some observation that has some physiological implausibility}
# ── Manual fixes for implausible values ───────────────────────────────────────
# patient "38f7f49b-6a5a-7717-3792-3a1d2518f66e" has HGB at 0 at day 10 and 16, and RBC at 0 at day 19
#remove all the observations for this patient in those days
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  filter(!(patient_id == "38f7f49b-6a5a-7717-3792-3a1d2518f66e" &
           day %in% c(10, 16,19)))
```

## Pre-fitting data conditioning

Two issues are addressed BEFORE the imputation step, both motivated by the
fact that natural cubic splines and smoothing splines are unconstrained
linear smoothers and can produce negative predictions on strictly
non-negative quantities (which is biologically nonsensical).

### Step 1 — Physiologically implausible zeros → NA

For a small set of haematological parameters, a value of 0 cannot occur in
a living patient (it would imply absence of red blood cells / haemoglobin)
and is almost certainly an instrument-read error. We coerce these to `NA`
so they do not anchor splines toward zero. Variables where 0 is biologically
plausible (e.g. eosinopenia → EOS = 0) are left untouched.

```{r physiological-zeros}
# Whitelist of biomarkers where 0 is physiologically impossible.
# Background: red-cell parameters (HCT, HGB, RBC) and red-cell indices
# (MCH, MCHC, MCV) are bounded well above zero in any living patient.
biomarkers_zero_implausible <- c(
  "HCT (%)", "HGB (g/dL)", "RBC (10^12/L)",
  "MCH (pg)", "MCHC (g/dL)", "MCV (fL)"
)

# Restrict to biomarkers actually in scope (BIOMARKERS_TO_USE may have
# excluded some of these — that's fine, they just don't need recoding).
biomarkers_zero_implausible <- intersect(biomarkers_zero_implausible, bio_cols)

if (length(biomarkers_zero_implausible) == 0) {
  cat("── No physiologically-implausible-zero biomarkers in current selection;",
      "skipping recoding step.\n")
} else {
  # Count zeros before, replace with NA, count after
  n_zeros_before <- df_clean %>%
    summarise(across(all_of(biomarkers_zero_implausible),
                     ~ sum(.x == 0, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "biomarker", values_to = "n_zeros") %>%
    filter(n_zeros > 0)

  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(biomarkers_zero_implausible),
                  ~ if_else(.x <= 0, NA_real_, .x)))

  cat("── Implausible zeros recoded as NA ─────────────────────────────────\n")
  print(n_zeros_before)
}
```

### Step 2 — Model choice: GAM with Gamma family and log link

All biomarkers are fitted with the same model: a Generalised Additive
Model (`mgcv::gam`) with Gamma response distribution and log link, on
the raw scale. The fit is performed independently for every
(patient × biomarker) combination.

**Why this single model**:

- **Structural non-negativity**. The log link gives
  $\hat\mu(t) = \exp(\eta(t)) > 0$ for any real value of the linear
  predictor $\eta(t)$. The fitted curve cannot dip below zero anywhere
  on the grid, not just at observed days. This removes the negativity
  problem that affected the earlier NCS / smoothing-spline approaches,
  without any post-hoc trick (no truncation, no response transform
  followed by back-transform).
- **Native heteroscedasticity**. The Gamma distribution satisfies
  $\text{Var}(Y) = \phi \mu^2$, i.e. variance scales with the squared
  mean. This matches the empirical pattern of CRP, LDH, transaminases
  (higher-mean patients have proportionally larger fluctuations) more
  faithfully than a homoscedastic Gaussian spline.
- **No back-transform bias**. The model targets $\mathbb{E}[Y]$ directly
  through the link; we do not compute $\exp(\mathbb{E}[\log Y])$, which
  would be biased (Duan 1983).
- **Single model, single code path**. A uniform choice across
  biomarkers makes the pipeline easier to reproduce and to document
  in the thesis.

**Exact zeros**. The Gamma family requires $Y > 0$ strictly. A small
number of biomarkers (EOS, LYM, MONO, NEU, PLT) can take the exact
value 0 legitimately (eosinopenia, lymphopenia, etc.). When these zeros
appear among the observations of a patient × biomarker combination,
`fit_gam_gamma` replaces them with $0.5 \times \min\{y : y > 0\}$
computed on that patient's observed values, before fitting. This is
the standard pragmatic device for Gamma / log-normal models with
zero observations.

**Basis dimension**. The smoothing-parameter λ is chosen automatically
by `mgcv` via REML (Wood 2011). The upper bound $k$ on the basis
dimension is adapted to the effective sample size:
$k = \min(6, \max(3, \lceil n/2 \rceil))$, where $n$ is the number of
points seen by the fit (observations plus anchor points). This
"more data → more knots" heuristic lets the fit capture more complex
trajectories when the data support it, while remaining stable for
patients with few measurements.

**Grid invariant**. Predictions are computed on the full
`GRID_DAYS = 0:14` (15 points) for every combination. The day-0 anchor
(always) and the day-14 anchor (for short-stay patients) ensure the
fit is stabilised at the grid boundaries; the penalised spline
interpolates inside and extrapolates smoothly outside the observed
range when necessary.

**Fallback**. When a patient × biomarker combination has fewer than
4 valid observations, the GAM is not fitted; LOCF (Last Observation
Carried Forward, with NOCB for leading missing days) is used instead.
LOCF is also used automatically whenever the GAM fit fails to
converge — an unlikely but possible event on very sparse data.

## Decision rules per patient × biomarker combination

| `n_valid` | `day_max`  | Routine                                  |
|-----------|------------|------------------------------------------|
| `< 4`     | any        | **LOCF** (universal fallback)            |
| `>= 4`    | `>= 14`    | **GAM Gamma** + day-0 anchor             |
| `>= 4`    | `< 14`     | **GAM Gamma** + day-0 anchor + day-14 anchor |

In all non-LOCF cases, the output is a length-15 vector on the raw
scale, guaranteed non-negative by construction of the log link.

```{r feasibility}
MIN_OBS <- 4L

feasibility <- df_clean %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(bio_cols),
               names_to = "biomarker", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(patient_id, biomarker) %>%
  summarise(
    n_valid    = sum(!is.na(value)),
    day_max_bm = if (any(!is.na(value))) max(day[!is.na(value)]) else 0L,
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(strategy = if_else(n_valid < MIN_OBS, "LOCF", "GAM"))

cat("=== Strategy distribution (patient × biomarker) ===\n")
feasibility %>%
  count(strategy) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  print()
```

```{r locf-plot, fig.height=6, fig.width=14}
locf_by_bm <- feasibility %>%
  filter(strategy == "LOCF") %>%
  count(biomarker, name = "n_LOCF") %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n_LOCF / length(eligible_ids), 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_LOCF))

locf_by_pat <- feasibility %>%
  filter(strategy == "LOCF") %>%
  count(patient_id, name = "n_LOCF_bm")

p1 <- ggplot(locf_by_bm,
             aes(x = reorder(biomarker, n_LOCF), y = n_LOCF)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct, "%")), hjust = -0.1, size = 2.8) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "LOCF by biomarker", x = NULL,
       y = "N patients with LOCF") +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(r = 50))

p1
```

# Fitting Functions

```{r functions}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# v7 fitting core: only two routines — LOCF (fallback for too-few-obs) and
# fit_gam_gamma (GAM with Gamma family + log link, used for every other
# (patient × biomarker) combination). Anchors are added by the dispatcher
# before handing data to the fitter, and predictions always cover the full
# GRID_DAYS (15 points).
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── LOCF ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Last Observation Carried Forward on the full grid. For days before the
# first observation, the first available value is used (NOCB).
# Used whenever n_valid < 4 for a (patient × biomarker) combination, or as
# an automatic fallback when the GAM fit fails to converge.
impute_locf <- function(days_obs, y_obs, days_grid) {
  ord      <- order(days_obs)
  days_obs <- days_obs[ord];  y_obs <- y_obs[ord]
  sapply(days_grid, function(d) {
    idx <- which(days_obs <= d & !is.na(y_obs))
    if (length(idx) == 0) {
      fv <- y_obs[!is.na(y_obs)]
      return(if (length(fv) == 0) NA_real_ else fv[1])
    }
    y_obs[max(idx)]
  })
}

# ── Anchor points ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stabilises the fit at grid boundaries by prepending / appending synthetic
# observations on the raw scale:
#   * day-0 anchor (always for GAM): (0, first_observed_value) if no day-0 obs.
#   * day-14 anchor (short-stay only): (14, mean_observed_value) if day_max < 14.
# This guarantees that GAM predictions on days_grid cover the full grid
# without relying on long extrapolation.
add_anchors <- function(d_obs, y_obs, GRID_MAX, day0 = TRUE, daymax = FALSE) {
  valid <- !is.na(y_obs)

  if (day0 && !0 %in% d_obs[valid]) {
    first_val <- y_obs[valid][which.min(d_obs[valid])]
    d_obs <- c(0,         d_obs)
    y_obs <- c(first_val, y_obs)
  }

  if (daymax) {
    mean_val <- mean(y_obs[!is.na(y_obs)])
    d_obs <- c(d_obs, GRID_MAX)
    y_obs <- c(y_obs, mean_val)
  }

  list(d = d_obs, y = y_obs)
}

# ── GAM fit with Gamma family and log link ────────────────────────────────────
# The one and only spline fitter in v7. Non-negativity is structural
# (mu = exp(eta) > 0), heteroscedasticity is native (Var(Y) = phi * mu^2),
# smoothness is selected automatically via REML.
#
# Design contract:
#   * Predicts on the FULL days_grid (length 15), always. Extrapolation
#     outside the observed range is handled smoothly by the penalised spline.
#   * Returns vectors of length length(days_grid), always. All outputs are
#     cast to plain atomic numeric vectors (strips names/matrix attributes
#     from predict.gam) so that downstream tibble + write_csv work cleanly.
#
# Arguments:
#   days_obs, y_obs : observed (anchor-augmented) days and values
#   days_grid       : prediction grid (full 0..14)
#   k_basis         : upper bound on basis dimension. mgcv penalises down to
#                     the effective complexity supported by the data.
fit_gam_gamma <- function(days_obs, y_obs, days_grid, k_basis = 4) {

  valid    <- !is.na(y_obs)
  days_fit <- days_obs[valid]
  y_fit    <- y_obs[valid]

  # ── Zero-jitter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Gamma family requires y > 0 strictly. Biomarkers with biologically valid
  # exact zeros (EOS, LYM, MONO, NEU, PLT) are handled here: each zero is
  # replaced with half the smallest positive value observed for this
  # (patient × biomarker) combination. Computed on-the-fly rather than
  # stored in a global table — this keeps the fitter self-contained.
  if (any(y_fit == 0)) {
    pos_vals <- y_fit[y_fit > 0]
    if (length(pos_vals) > 0) {
      y_fit[y_fit == 0] <- 0.5 * min(pos_vals)
    } else {
      # Pathological edge case: all values are zero. Push everything off
      # zero by a tiny amount so the Gamma likelihood is defined.
      y_fit[y_fit == 0] <- 1e-6
    }
  }
  # Final safety (defensive against negatives)
  if (any(y_fit <= 0)) {
    eps <- 0.5 * min(y_fit[y_fit > 0])
    y_fit[y_fit <= 0] <- eps
  }

  tryCatch({
    # Cap k at n_unique - 1 (mgcv requires k < n_unique)
    k_use <- min(k_basis, length(unique(days_fit)) - 1)
    if (k_use < 3) stop("not enough unique days for k >= 3")

    # bs = "cr" : cubic regression spline basis
    # method = "REML" : stable smoothness selection (Wood 2011)
    fit_obj <- gam(y_fit ~ s(days_fit, bs = "cr", k = k_use),
                   family = Gamma(link = "log"),
                   method = "REML")

    # Predict on the full grid, on the link (log) scale, with SE.
    # Symmetric CI on the link scale → asymmetric CI on raw scale after
    # back-transform, which is the correct behaviour for log-link models.
    pred <- predict(fit_obj,
                    newdata = data.frame(days_fit = days_grid),
                    type    = "link",
                    se.fit  = TRUE)

    eta_hat <- as.numeric(pred$fit)      # strip names / matrix attrs
    se_eta  <- as.numeric(pred$se.fit)

    fit <- as.numeric(exp(eta_hat))
    lwr <- as.numeric(exp(eta_hat - 2 * se_eta))
    upr <- as.numeric(exp(eta_hat + 2 * se_eta))
    # SE on response scale via delta method (diagnostic only)
    se  <- as.numeric(fit * se_eta)

    list(fit    = fit,
         se     = se,
         lwr    = lwr,
         upr    = upr,
         method = "GAM_Gamma_log")

  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(sprintf("GAM Gamma failed (k=%d): %s", k_basis, e$message))
    locf <- impute_locf(days_obs, y_obs, days_grid)
    list(fit = as.numeric(locf),
         se  = rep(NA_real_, length(days_grid)),
         lwr = rep(NA_real_, length(days_grid)),
         upr = rep(NA_real_, length(days_grid)),
         method = "LOCF_fallback")
  })
}

# ── Master dispatcher ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Routing logic:
#   strategy == "LOCF" → impute_locf (and we're done)
#   strategy == "GAM"  → add day-0 anchor; if day_max_bm < 14 also add day-14
#                        anchor; then fit_gam_gamma
# n_fit (observations + anchors) determines the k cap: k = min(6, max(3, ceil(n/2))).
impute_one <- function(pid, bm, df_clean, feasibility, GRID_DAYS, GRID_MAX) {

  pat   <- df_clean %>% filter(patient_id == pid) %>% arrange(day)
  y_obs <- pat[[bm]]
  d_obs <- pat$day

  feas <- feasibility %>% filter(patient_id == pid, biomarker == bm)
  strat      <- if (nrow(feas) == 0) "LOCF" else feas$strategy
  day_max_bm <- if (nrow(feas) == 0) 0L     else feas$day_max_bm

  # ── LOCF ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (strat == "LOCF") {
    locf <- impute_locf(d_obs, y_obs, GRID_DAYS)
    return(list(fit    = as.numeric(locf),
                se     = rep(NA_real_, length(GRID_DAYS)),
                lwr    = rep(NA_real_, length(GRID_DAYS)),
                upr    = rep(NA_real_, length(GRID_DAYS)),
                method = "LOCF"))
  }

  # ── GAM Gamma + log link ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Day-0 anchor always; day-14 anchor only if the patient's data don't
  # already reach the end of the grid.
  need_daymax_anchor <- day_max_bm < GRID_MAX
  anch  <- add_anchors(d_obs, y_obs, GRID_MAX,
                       day0   = TRUE,
                       daymax = need_daymax_anchor)
  d_fit <- anch$d;  y_fit <- anch$y

  n_fit <- sum(!is.na(y_fit))
  k_use <- min(6, max(3, ceiling(n_fit / 2)))

  fit_gam_gamma(d_fit, y_fit, GRID_DAYS, k_basis = k_use)
}
```

# Main Imputation Loop

```{r imputation-loop, cache=TRUE}
records_main   <- vector("list", length(eligible_ids))
records_spline <- vector("list", length(eligible_ids) * length(bio_cols))
spline_idx     <- 1L

for (i in seq_along(eligible_ids)) {
  pid <- eligible_ids[i]

  bio_matrix <- matrix(NA_real_,
                       nrow = length(GRID_DAYS),
                       ncol = length(bio_cols),
                       dimnames = list(NULL, bio_cols))

  for (j in seq_along(bio_cols)) {
    bm  <- bio_cols[j]
    res <- impute_one(pid, bm, df_clean, feasibility, GRID_DAYS, GRID_MAX)

    bio_matrix[, j] <- as.numeric(res$fit)

    if (!startsWith(res$method, "LOCF")) {
      # Defensive: force fit/se/lwr/upr to plain atomic numeric vectors.
      # Some fitters (e.g. mgcv::predict.gam) may return named vectors or
      # single-column matrices that would become list/matrix columns in
      # the tibble and break readr::write_csv downstream.
      records_spline[[spline_idx]] <- tibble(
        patient_id = pid,
        day        = GRID_DAYS,
        biomarker  = bm,
        fit        = as.numeric(res$fit),
        se         = as.numeric(res$se),
        lwr        = as.numeric(res$lwr),
        upr        = as.numeric(res$upr),
        method     = res$method
      )
      spline_idx <- spline_idx + 1L
    }
  }

  records_main[[i]] <- bind_cols(
    tibble(patient_id = pid, day = GRID_DAYS),
    as_tibble(bio_matrix)
  )
}

cat("Loop complete.\n")
```

```{r assemble-main}
df_main <- bind_rows(records_main) %>%
  left_join(admission_covs, by = "patient_id") %>%
  # ── Per-day in-hospital is_dead flag ─────────────────────────────────────
  # 1 from the day of death onwards, 0 before. Always 0 for living patients
  # (days_death_from_admission == -1 sentinel). Note that with the grid
  # capped at day 14, in-hospital death is only visible inside the grid
  # when it occurred within the first 14 days of admission.
  mutate(
    is_dead = if_else(
      days_death_from_admission >= 0L & day >= days_death_from_admission,
      1L, 0L
    )
  ) %>%
  select(patient_id, day, all_of(bio_cols), all_of(cov_cols), is_dead)

cat("Main output:", nrow(df_main), "rows ×", ncol(df_main), "cols\n")
cat("Time points per patient:", n_distinct(df_main$day),
    "(day 0 –", max(df_main$day), ")\n")
cat("Patient-days flagged is_dead == 1:", sum(df_main$is_dead), "\n")
glimpse(df_main)

## CRP–WBC discordance channel D(t)

```{r add-discordance-channel}
# ── Point 2: synthetic infection channel from CRP/WBC trend discordance ──────
# Directional contrast of the standardized 2-day BACKWARD log-changes:
#     D(t) = z(Δ log1p CRP) − z(Δ log1p WBC)
# Large & positive when CRP RISES while WBC FALLS (the infective pattern the
# clinicians flagged), minimal in the opposite case, ~0 when concordant.
# Computed on the imputed regular grid (df_main = smooth GAM fit), on the log1p
# scale so the change is a scale-stable log fold-change (CRP is heavily skewed).
# D can be negative → it is deliberately NOT added to bio_cols, so it is never
# log1p-transformed downstream and is skipped by the non-negativity check.
# Backward (not centred) difference → future-leak-free and aligned with the
# 2-day alert cadence used in the post-hoc notebook.
INFECTION_ADD_D    <- FALSE
INFECTION_CRP_COL  <- "CRP (mg/L)"
INFECTION_WBC_COL  <- "WBC (10^9/L)"
INFECTION_D_NAME   <- "CRP-WBC discordance"
INFECTION_LAG_DAYS <- 2L

if (INFECTION_ADD_D) {
  miss <- setdiff(c(INFECTION_CRP_COL, INFECTION_WBC_COL), names(df_main))
  if (length(miss) > 0)
    stop("D(t) needs imputed CRP and WBC in df_main. Missing: ",
         paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
         ". Add them to BIOMARKERS_TO_USE and re-run from the top.")

  df_main <- df_main %>%
    arrange(patient_id, day) %>%
    group_by(patient_id) %>%
    mutate(
      .lcrp = log1p(.data[[INFECTION_CRP_COL]]),
      .lwbc = log1p(.data[[INFECTION_WBC_COL]]),
      .dCRP = .lcrp - dplyr::lag(.lcrp, INFECTION_LAG_DAYS),
      .dWBC = .lwbc - dplyr::lag(.lwbc, INFECTION_LAG_DAYS)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  .sCRP <- sd(df_main$.dCRP, na.rm = TRUE)
  .sWBC <- sd(df_main$.dWBC, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(.sCRP) || .sCRP == 0 || !is.finite(.sWBC) || .sWBC == 0)
    stop("Zero/undefined SD for the CRP or WBC 2-day change — cannot standardize D(t).")

  d_vec <- (df_main$.dCRP / .sCRP) - (df_main$.dWBC / .sWBC)
  d_vec[is.na(d_vec)] <- 0            # days 0..(lag-1) have no 2-day history
  df_main[[INFECTION_D_NAME]] <- d_vec

  # Drop the scratch columns and pin a stable column order:
  # id/day → biomarkers → D → covariates → is_dead
  df_main <- df_main %>%
    select(-.lcrp, -.lwbc, -.dCRP, -.dWBC) %>%
    select(patient_id, day, all_of(bio_cols),
           all_of(INFECTION_D_NAME), all_of(cov_cols), is_dead)

  cat(sprintf("D(t) channel '%s' added (lag = %d days). Range [%.2f, %.2f]; SD = %.3f\n",
              INFECTION_D_NAME, INFECTION_LAG_DAYS,
              min(df_main[[INFECTION_D_NAME]]), max(df_main[[INFECTION_D_NAME]]),
              sd(df_main[[INFECTION_D_NAME]])))
} else {
  cat("INFECTION_ADD_D = FALSE → D(t) channel not created.\n")
}
```

```{r negativity-check}
# Sanity check: count negative imputed values per biomarker.
# With log1p + zero-jitter, this should be exactly zero everywhere.
neg_counts <- df_main %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(bio_cols), names_to = "biomarker", values_to = "v") %>%
  group_by(biomarker) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total    = sum(!is.na(v)),
    n_negative = sum(v < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_zero     = sum(v == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_value  = min(v, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_negative))

cat("── Post-imputation negativity check ────────────────────────────────\n")
print(neg_counts, n = length(bio_cols))

if (sum(neg_counts$n_negative) == 0) {
  cat("\nNo negative imputed values anywhere - non-negativity holds.\n")
} else {
  cat("\nWARNING:", sum(neg_counts$n_negative),
      "negative imputed values found across",
      sum(neg_counts$n_negative > 0), "biomarkers.\n")
  cat("  With GAM Gamma + log link this should not happen — investigate.\n")
}

# Diagnostic Plots

## Plot function

- **Red circles** – observed values
- **Blue solid** – NCS fit (within observed range), **±2 SE ribbon** (asymmetric if log-transformed)
- **Blue dashed** – linear tail (NCS edge case beyond last obs, rare)
- **Green solid** – SS_df4 fit (full grid, includes both anchors), **±2 SE ribbon**
- **Orange solid** – LOCF
- **Grey dashed vertical** – day 14 (grid end)
- **Filled triangle** – synthetic anchor point(s) used in fitting

Note: when log-transform is active, the CI ribbon is asymmetric (wider above,
narrower below the fit line), which is the correct behaviour for a log-normal
back-transform. Fitted values are always non-negative.

```{r plot-function}
plot_one <- function(df_raw, df_spline_long, pid, bm, GRID_DAYS,
                     y_limits = NULL) {

  obs <- df_raw %>%
    filter(patient_id == pid) %>%
    select(day, value = all_of(bm)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(value))

  sp <- df_spline_long %>%
    filter(patient_id == pid, biomarker == bm)

  is_spline <- nrow(sp) > 0
  strat     <- if (is_spline) unique(sp$method) else "LOCF"
  is_gam    <- startsWith(strat, "GAM")

  # Short-stay (day-14 anchor was added) is detected from the observed data,
  # since the method string itself doesn't encode it.
  obs_day_max <- if (nrow(obs) > 0) max(obs$day) else NA_real_
  is_gam_short <- is_gam && !is.na(obs_day_max) &&
                  obs_day_max < max(GRID_DAYS)

  # LOCF reconstruction (no spline data available for this combination)
  if (!is_spline) {
    pat  <- df_raw %>% filter(patient_id == pid)
    locf <- impute_locf(pat$day, pat[[bm]], GRID_DAYS)
    sp   <- tibble(day = GRID_DAYS, fit = locf,
                   se = NA_real_, lwr = NA_real_, upr = NA_real_)
  }

  # Anchor markers (day-0 for any GAM; day-14 for short-stay GAM)
  anchors <- tibble(day = numeric(), val = numeric(), type = character())
  if (is_spline) {
    real_obs <- obs
    if (nrow(real_obs) > 0 && min(real_obs$day) > 0) {
      anchors <- bind_rows(anchors,
                           tibble(day  = 0,
                                  val  = real_obs$value[which.min(real_obs$day)],
                                  type = "day-0 anchor"))
    }
    if (is_gam_short) {
      y_vals <- df_raw %>% filter(patient_id == pid) %>% pull(all_of(bm))
      anchors <- bind_rows(anchors,
                           tibble(day  = max(GRID_DAYS),
                                  val  = mean(y_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
                                  type = "day-14 anchor"))
    }
  }

  col_gam  <- "#8e44ad"   # purple for GAM Gamma + log link
  col_locf <- "darkorange"

  p <- ggplot()

  # Ribbon (GAM only — LOCF has no CI)
  if (is_gam && any(!is.na(sp$lwr)))
    p <- p + geom_ribbon(data = sp,
                         aes(x = day, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr),
                         fill = col_gam, alpha = 0.18)

  # Fitted line
  if (is_gam)
    p <- p + geom_line(data = sp, aes(x = day, y = fit),
                       color = col_gam, linewidth = 0.9)
  if (!is_spline)
    p <- p + geom_line(data = sp, aes(x = day, y = fit),
                       color = col_locf, linewidth = 0.9)

  # Observed points
  p <- p + geom_point(data = obs, aes(x = day, y = value),
                      color = "red", size = 1.2, shape = 19)

  # Anchor markers
  if (nrow(anchors) > 0)
    p <- p + geom_point(data = anchors, aes(x = day, y = val),
                        shape = 17, size = 2, color = "grey30")

  p <- p +
    geom_vline(xintercept = max(GRID_DAYS), linetype = "dashed",
               color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
    labs(title    = bm,
         subtitle = strat,
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          plot.title    = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7))

  if (!is.null(y_limits))
    p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits, xlim = range(GRID_DAYS))

  p
}
```

## Sample of 12 patients – per biomarker {.unnumbered}


```{r sample-plots}
FIG_DIR <- "figures"
dir.create(FIG_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)

TW      <- 5.51   # inches = 140 mm. Replace with your \the\textwidth if different.
N_PANEL <- 12
N_LOCF  <- 2      # fallback cases to force into each grid

fig_files <- c("HGB (g/dL)"   = "gam_sample_hgb.pdf",
               "CREA (mg/dL)" = "gam_sample_crea.pdf",
               "ALT (U/L)"    = "gam_sample_alt.pdf")

for (bm in bio_cols) {

  # --- panel selection: force N_LOCF fallback cases, fill the rest with GAM ---
  gam_ids_bm  <- df_spline %>% filter(biomarker == bm) %>%
                 pull(patient_id) %>% unique()
  locf_ids_bm <- setdiff(eligible_ids, gam_ids_bm)

  set.seed(1)
  n_locf  <- min(N_LOCF, length(locf_ids_bm))
  pick_lo <- locf_ids_bm[sample.int(length(locf_ids_bm), n_locf)]
  pick_ga <- gam_ids_bm[ sample.int(length(gam_ids_bm),  N_PANEL - n_locf)]
  ids_bm  <- c(pick_lo, pick_ga)

  # --- common y range across the panels of this biomarker ---
  all_obs <- df_clean %>% filter(patient_id %in% ids_bm) %>%
             pull(all_of(bm)) %>% na.omit()
  all_fit <- df_spline %>% filter(patient_id %in% ids_bm, biomarker == bm) %>%
             pull(fit)
  y_lim <- quantile(c(all_obs, all_fit), probs = c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)

  # --- build panels; drop the per-panel biomarker title, keep the method ---
  pl_bm <- lapply(ids_bm, function(pid)
    plot_one(df_clean, df_spline, pid, bm, GRID_DAYS, y_limits = y_lim) +
      labs(title = NULL))

  pw <- wrap_plots(pl_bm, ncol = 3) &
        theme_bw(base_size = 8) &
        theme(legend.position  = "none",
              plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 6.5),
              panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
              plot.margin      = margin(2, 2, 2, 2))

  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, fig_files[[bm]]), pw,
         width = TW, height = 6.2, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)

  cat(sprintf("saved %s  (%d LOCF panels)\n", fig_files[[bm]], n_locf))
  print(pw)
  cat("\n\n\\newpage\n\n")
}

# Outlier Analysis

This section investigates the heavy tails present in the biomarker distributions.

**Strategies compared:**

| # | Transform | Outlier criterion |
|---|-----------|-------------------|
| 1 | None (raw) | outside \[Q1 − 3·IQR, Q3 + 3·IQR\] on raw scale |
| 2 | log(x) | outside \[Q1 − 3·IQR, Q3 + 3·IQR\] on log scale |
| 3 | log(log(x)) | outside \[Q1 − 3·IQR, Q3 + 3·IQR\] on log-log scale |

A patient is removed under a strategy if **at least one** of their measurements
(across all biomarkers) is flagged as an outlier.

**Notes on applicability:**

- **log(x)** requires all values > 0; biomarkers that include 0 or negatives
  are excluded from this comparison and marked as `NA`.
- **log(log(x))** additionally requires all values > 1 (so that log(x) > 0);
  biomarkers failing this are also marked `NA`.




```{r outlier-helper}
# Flag values outside k × IQR from Q1/Q3; returns logical vector
flag_outliers_iqr <- function(x, k = 3) {
  q   <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q[2] - q[1]
  if (iqr == 0) return(rep(FALSE, length(x)))   # constant biomarker → no outliers
  (x < q[1] - k * iqr) | (x > q[2] + k * iqr)
}
```

```{r outlier-per-biomarker}
# Long format (eligible patients only, observed values only)
bio_long_clean <- df_clean %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(bio_cols),
               names_to = "biomarker", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value))

# Per-biomarker: check feasibility of each transform
bm_outlier_info <- bio_long_clean %>%
  group_by(biomarker) %>%
  summarise(
    n_obs      = n(),
    min_val    = min(value),
    max_val    = max(value),
    can_log1p  = all(value >= 0),   # log1p  x ≥ 0
    can_loglog = all(value > 0),    # for log(log1p(x)) needs log1p(x) > 0 → x > 0
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

# Flag outliers on each scale, per biomarker
outlier_flags <- bio_long_clean %>%
  left_join(bm_outlier_info %>% select(biomarker, can_log1p, can_loglog),
            by = "biomarker") %>%
  group_by(biomarker) %>%
  mutate(
    outlier_raw = flag_outliers_iqr(value),

    outlier_log1p = if (first(can_log1p)) 
      flag_outliers_iqr(log1p(value)) 
    else NA,

    outlier_loglog = if (first(can_loglog)) 
      flag_outliers_iqr(log(log1p(value))) 
    else NA
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r outlier-patient-counts}
# Helper: unique patients flagged under a given column
n_patients_flagged <- function(col) {
  outlier_flags %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[col]]) & .data[[col]]) %>%
    pull(patient_id) %>%
    n_distinct()
}

n_raw    <- n_patients_flagged("outlier_raw")
n_log    <- n_patients_flagged("outlier_log1p")
n_loglog <- n_patients_flagged("outlier_loglog")

cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("   OUTLIER REMOVAL IMPACT — patients that WOULD be excluded\n")
cat("   (based on ≥1 measurement outside 3×IQR on the stated scale)\n")
cat("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
tibble(
  Strategy          = c("Raw (no transform)",
                         "Log scale  [log1p(x); only if x >= 0]",
                         "Log-log scale [log(log1p(x)); only if x > 0]"),
  Patients_removed  = c(n_raw, n_log, n_loglog),
  Pct_of_eligible   = sprintf("%.1f%%",
                               100 * c(n_raw, n_log, n_loglog) / length(eligible_ids))
) %>% print()
```

```{r outlier-per-biomarker-table}
# Per-biomarker breakdown: how many patients are flagged per strategy?
bm_outlier_summary <- outlier_flags %>%
  group_by(biomarker) %>%
  summarise(
    n_measures       = n(),
    n_patients       = n_distinct(patient_id),
    # Raw
    n_flag_raw       = sum(outlier_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_flag_raw     = round(100 * n_flag_raw / n_measures, 1),
    # Log
    can_log1p          = first(can_log1p),
    n_flag_log1p       = sum(outlier_log1p,    na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_flag_log1p     = round(100 * n_flag_log1p / n_measures, 1),
    # Log-log
    can_loglog       = first(can_loglog),
    n_flag_loglog    = sum(outlier_loglog, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_flag_loglog  = round(100 * n_flag_loglog / n_measures, 1),
    .groups          = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_flag_log1p    = if_else(can_log1p,    pct_flag_log1p,    NA_real_),
    pct_flag_loglog = if_else(can_loglog, pct_flag_loglog, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  select(-can_log1p, -can_loglog) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_flag_raw))

cat("\n── Per-biomarker outlier rates (% of measurements flagged) ──\n")
print(bm_outlier_summary, n = length(bio_cols))
```

# Distribution plots: raw vs log vs log-log for each biomarker
# Show one representative plot per biomarker (histogram + 3×IQR bounds)
# Distribution plots: RAW scale for each biomarker
# One plot per biomarker (histogram + 3×IQR bounds)

bm_dist_plots <- lapply(bio_cols, function(bm) {

  bm_info <- bm_outlier_info %>% filter(biomarker == bm)

  # Extract raw values
  vals <- bio_long_clean %>%
    filter(biomarker == bm) %>%
    pull(value)

  # Compute IQR bounds on RAW scale
  q   <- quantile(vals, c(0.25, 0.75))
  iqr <- q[2] - q[1]
  lo  <- q[1] - 3 * iqr
  hi  <- q[2] + 3 * iqr

  # Plot histogram with outlier bounds
  ggplot(tibble(x = vals), aes(x = x)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(lo, hi),
               color = "red",
               linetype = "dashed",
               linewidth = 0.6) +
    labs(
      title = bm,
      subtitle = sprintf("RAW scale | 3×IQR bounds: [%.2g, %.2g]", lo, hi),
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6)
    )
})

# Print 12 plots per page
n_pages <- ceiling(length(bio_cols) / 12)

for (pg in seq_len(n_pages)) {

  idx <- ((pg - 1) * 12 + 1):min(pg * 12, length(bio_cols))

                        pg, n_pages),

        theme = theme(
          plot.title    = element_text(size = 11),

        )
      )
  )

  cat("\n\n\\newpage\n\n")
}

# Distribution plots: LOG1P scale for each biomarker
# Same structure as RAW, but computed on log1p(x)

bm_dist_plots_log <- lapply(bio_cols, function(bm) {

  bm_info <- bm_outlier_info %>% filter(biomarker == bm)

  # Extract raw values
  vals <- bio_long_clean %>%
    filter(biomarker == bm) %>%
    pull(value)

  # Skip biomarkers with negative values (log1p not defined)
  if (!bm_info$can_log1p) return(NULL)

  # Apply log1p transformation
  vals_log <- log1p(vals)

  # Compute IQR bounds on LOG1P scale
  q   <- quantile(vals_log, c(0.25, 0.75))
  iqr <- q[2] - q[1]
  lo  <- q[1] - 3 * iqr
  hi  <- q[2] + 3 * iqr

  # Plot histogram
  ggplot(tibble(x = vals_log), aes(x = x)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#55A868", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(lo, hi),
               color = "#C44E52",
               linetype = "dashed",
               linewidth = 0.6) +
    labs(
      title = bm,
      subtitle = sprintf("log1p scale | 3×IQR bounds: [%.2g, %.2g]", lo, hi),
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6)
    )
})

# Remove NULL entries (non-compatible biomarkers)
bm_dist_plots_log <- bm_dist_plots_log[!sapply(bm_dist_plots_log, is.null)]

# Print 12 plots per page
n_pages_log <- ceiling(length(bm_dist_plots_log) / 12)

for (pg in seq_len(n_pages_log)) {

  idx <- ((pg - 1) * 12 + 1):min(pg * 12, length(bm_dist_plots_log))

  print(
    wrap_plots(bm_dist_plots_log[idx], ncol = 4) +
      plot_annotation(
        title = sprintf("LOG1P distribution + 3×IQR outlier bounds (%d/%d)",
                        pg, n_pages_log),
        subtitle = "Transform: log1p(x) | Red dashed lines = Q1−3×IQR and Q3+3×IQR",
        theme = theme(
          plot.title    = element_text(size = 11),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
        )
      )
  )

  cat("\n\n\\newpage\n\n")
}

# Downstream-Ready Dataset: Skewness-Based log1p Transform

```{r log1p-transform-for-downstream}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Downstream-ready dataset: apply log1p to heavily skewed biomarkers so the
# HMM / clustering / outlier detection downstream sees distributions closer
# to symmetric.
#
# Decision rule: log1p is applied to a biomarker iff sample skewness on the
# IMPUTED values (df_main) exceeds SKEW_THRESHOLD_LOG. Skewness is computed
# on raw-scale imputed values, which are guaranteed positive (so log1p is
# always defined).
#
# IMPORTANT — for clinical interpretation:
#   The raw-scale CSV (df_imputed_wide.csv) stays unchanged. The log1p
#   version is saved as a SEPARATE file (df_imputed_wide_log1p.csv). A
#   decision table documenting which biomarkers were transformed is saved
#   as bm_log1p_decisions.csv. When interpreting any downstream output
#   (states, trajectories, clusters) that used the log1p-transformed
#   biomarkers, remember to back-transform with expm1() to return to the
#   original clinical units (e.g. mg/L for CRP, U/L for LDH, etc.).
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SKEW_THRESHOLD_LOG <- 1.0   # |skew| above which log1p is applied

# Sample skewness (Fisher-Pearson, bias-corrected) on imputed values
.sample_skewness <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  if (n < 3) return(NA_real_)
  m <- mean(x); s <- sd(x)
  if (s == 0) return(0)
  (n / ((n - 1) * (n - 2))) * sum(((x - m) / s)^3)
}

# Skewness per biomarker on the IMPUTED dataset (df_main, raw scale)
bm_log1p_decisions <- tibble(biomarker = bio_cols) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    skew_imputed = .sample_skewness(df_main[[biomarker]]),
    apply_log1p  = is.finite(skew_imputed) &&
                   abs(skew_imputed) > SKEW_THRESHOLD_LOG
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(apply_log1p), desc(abs(skew_imputed)))

cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat("   log1p transform decisions for the DOWNSTREAM-READY dataset\n")
cat("══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n")
cat(sprintf("Threshold: |skew| > %g\n\n", SKEW_THRESHOLD_LOG))
print(bm_log1p_decisions, n = length(bio_cols))

bm_log1p <- bm_log1p_decisions %>%
  filter(apply_log1p) %>%
  pull(biomarker)

cat("\n── Biomarkers that WILL be log1p-transformed ────────────────────────\n")
if (length(bm_log1p) == 0) {
  cat("(none)\n")
} else {
  for (bm in bm_log1p) cat("  -", bm, "\n")
}
cat(sprintf("\nTotal: %d / %d biomarkers transformed\n",
            length(bm_log1p), length(bio_cols)))

# Build the log1p-transformed dataset. Only the selected biomarkers are
# transformed; the rest are left on raw scale. ID and covariate columns
# are preserved untouched.
df_main_log1p <- df_main %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(bm_log1p), log1p))

# Sanity check: no NaN / Inf introduced by log1p (shouldn't happen since
# imputed values are strictly positive, but worth checking)
sanity_bad <- df_main_log1p %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(bm_log1p),
                   ~ sum(!is.finite(.x) & !is.na(.x)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "biomarker", values_to = "n_bad") %>%
  filter(n_bad > 0)

if (nrow(sanity_bad) > 0) {
  cat("\nWARNING: log1p produced non-finite values in some biomarkers:\n")
  print(sanity_bad)
} else {
  cat("\nlog1p applied cleanly (no NaN/Inf introduced)\n")
}

# Save the three files:
#   1. bm_log1p_decisions.csv — which biomarkers were transformed and why
#   2. df_imputed_wide.csv    — raw-scale, unchanged (re-saved for safety)
#   3. df_imputed_wide_log1p.csv — log1p applied to the flagged biomarkers
write_csv(bm_log1p_decisions, "bm_log1p_decisions.csv")
write_csv(df_main,            "df_imputed_wide.csv")
write_csv(df_main_log1p,      "df_imputed_wide_log1p.csv")

cat("\n── Files saved ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
cat("  bm_log1p_decisions.csv    (decision table)\n")
cat("  df_imputed_wide.csv       (raw scale, unchanged)\n")
cat("  df_imputed_wide_log1p.csv (log1p applied to flagged biomarkers)\n")
```
